newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices again lifted by heat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices again lifted by heat.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were steady to slightly higher again Tuesday in quiet trade, with a blistering heat wave in the East still keeping sellers in control though buyers were not scrambling for supply.

"There's no reason for prices to come down with this heat. Sellers are digging their heels in," said one cash trader, noting some grades of resid were more competitive after this week's rally in city gate gas prices.
Temperatures in the East are forecast to remain above-normal for most of the week, but more seasonal weather is expected for the weekend and next week.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent firmed 20 cents to about the $16.75 a barrel area, with August one percent paper jumping 30 to 40 cents to about $16.50 after the sharp rebound in crude, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour sellers raised their sights by 10 cents to $18, but traders said reports of some West African material due later this month kept buyers fairly relaxed.
High sulphurs in New York again held steady, with 2.2 percent still pegged in the low-$15s.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with one percent still in the low-$16s and three percent at $14.25-50.
A 1.5 percent (10.5 gravity) USG sale was reported at $14.40 but the deal was not confirmed.

New York city gate swing gas jumped another nickel or more Tuesday to the low-$2.50s/mmBtu, or $15.94 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed a couple of cents to $2.20/mmBtu, or $13.86 a barrel.
